Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp.'s Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are John Ramirez, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Operating Officer; David Kwon, VP of Exploration; Elena Vasquez, VP of Marketing; and Tom Reilly, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to John Ramirez.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp. delivered solid results in Q2, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices with Brent averaging $82 per barrel and WTI at $78. We made significant strides in managing our debt levels, bringing total debt down meaningfully while improving leverage ratios. Our EBITDA saw robust growth year-over-year, fueled by higher realizations and volume increases. We're executing our capital allocation priorities effectively, balancing dividends, buybacks, and high-return reinvestments. We've refined our capital expenditure guidance to support sustained returns. The midstream segment performed resiliently with record transportation volumes and key infrastructure advancements. We achieved strong proved reserves additions, boasting an impressive reserve replacement ratio through organic efforts. Finally, we're advancing ESG initiatives, particularly on emissions reductions. Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Mike Chen: Thank you, John. As John mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $5.6 billion, up 28% year-over-year. Operating income was $1.9 billion, and net income was $1.3 billion. We generated $1.6 billion in free cash flow and returned $950 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $14.8 billion in total debt and $2.4 billion in cash.

Let me provide some additional color on our debt profile, which continues to highlight the strength and flexibility of our balance sheet in this volatile oil and gas environment. We've prioritized deleveraging while keeping ample liquidity for our high-return drilling in the Permian and Eagle Ford. Total debt ended Q2 at $14.8 billion, down $1.2 billion from year-end 2023, thanks to disciplined allocation including $850 million in paydowns from operational cash flows and the $2.1 billion divestiture of non-core Bakken assets closed in April. Our debt mix is investment-grade: 55% fixed-rate senior notes maturing 2026-2042 at a 4.8% blended coupon, 30% on our $4 billion revolver with only $500 million drawn, and the rest in term loans and leases. Weighted average cost is 4.6%, below peers like Occidental's 5.2%, with no major maturities until 2026.

Net debt, total debt minus cash and equivalents, was $12.4 billion, our lowest since 2019, reduced $1.5 billion quarter-over-quarter from $1.8 billion operating cash flow, partially offset by working capital in the Gulf of Mexico. That's 18% deleveraging year-over-year from $15.2 billion, outpacing Chevron and targeting sub-$12 billion by end-2025. Leverage, net debt to LTM EBITDAX, improved to 1.6x from 2.1x, at the low end of our 1.5x-2.0x range, with LTM EBITDAX at $7.8 billion from 12% production growth to 650 Mboe/d, Permian efficiencies dropping LOE 8% to $6/boe, and strong NGL pricing. This beats EOG at 0.8x, Pioneer at 1.2x, and Conoco at 1.4x; debt-to-capital is 28% versus 35% last year. Covenant headroom is solid: 4.1x on RBL versus 3.25x threshold, interest coverage 8.2x over 4x.

In the Permian Delaware, 120 wells with 11,000-foot laterals and 55 frac stages yielded 25% FCF to capex, cutting net debt $400 million. Eagle Ford added $250 million, hedged against $2.40 NYMEX gas. GoM Shenzi North tie-backs are breakeven at $60 Brent with subsea tech slowing declines 15%. We sold our Suriname Block 58 stake for $300 million to focus domestic. We're returning 50% FCF via $1.20/share dividend (3.8% yield) and $2 billion buyback, with $750 million repurchased YTD. AI frac in Midland boosts EURs 20% to 1.2 Mboe/well, centralized procurement saves $150 million yearly, supporting $4-5 billion FCF in 2024 at $80 Brent. Net debt should dip below $11.5 billion by Q4 at 1.4x leverage.

Turning to adjusted EBITDA, it hit $2.1 billion for the quarter, up 42% from $1.48 billion in Q2 2023, with TTM at $8.4 billion, up 45% YoY. Realized pricing added $1.2 billion YoY: upstream oil at $78.50/bbl up 52%, gas $3.25/Mcf, NGLs $28.10/bbl up 38%, 85% oil hedged at $70 floor. Production rose 12% to 525,000 boe/d, adding $650 million; Permian up 18% to 320,000 boe/d on 45-rig program with 12,000-foot laterals, 2,500 lbs/ft proppant, IP rates over 1,200 boe/d outperforming type curves 15%; Eagle Ford +8% to 95,000 boe/d; GoM flat at 65,000; North Sea down 5% to 45,000 with $200 million CO2 EOR at Magnus for 10% uplift.

Costs contributed $380 million: LOE down 16% to $8.20/boe via digital twins and AI maintenance cutting downtime 22%; DD&A $14.50/boe on 8% decline rate; G&A down 10% post-merger. Midstream Apex Express at 800,000 bbl/d captured $2.50/bbl tolls up from $1.80; Houston refining $18/bbl cracks. U.S. onshore drove 70%, Permian D&C at $450/foot; international Guyana PSC for 50,000 boe/d at $30/boe breakeven. FY2024 EBITDA guided $8.5-9.0 billion.

On capital allocation, with $4.2 billion FCF in first nine months up 25% at $82 WTI/$86 Brent, priorities are dividends first at 40-50% FCF payout: Q3 $0.65/share for FY $2.60 up 12%, 4.2% yield covering 2.5x at $50 WTI, backed by Permian 60% IRR, Brazil Buzios $35 breakeven, ADNOC Ruwais 150 Mbbl/d. 2025 dividends $1.8 billion, potential 10% hike. Buybacks second: $3 billion authorized, $1.7 billion YTD retiring 4.2% shares at $62 vs. $95 NAV, adding $0.45 to 2025 EPS; tactical on dips, 75% FCF returns total. Reinvestment 25% or $1 billion: >20% IRR, Permian $800 million for 120 wells Wolfcamp C 12,000-foot laterals AI-optimized 1.2 MBOE EURs; Brazil/Guyana $300 million; LNG $200 million Golden Pass/Corpus; low-carbon $100 million CCUS Permian/Oxy DAC 1 Mtpa, Bakken electrification for IRA credits. Debt paydown $500 million YTD to <$5 billion. Framework 50% dividends/25% buybacks/25% reinvest for 12-15% yield, 3% production CAGR.

For capex, YTD $2.5 billion at 70% upstream D&C, Q2 18 rigs Permian. Raised FY2024 to $2.6-2.8 billion for 15-20 extra wells, FCF $1.2 billion at $75 WTI/$4 gas. 2025 $2.7-2.9 billion flat, 110-120 wells to 180-190k BOE/d 65% oil: 75% D&C, 10% maintenance/midstream/low-carbon. Permian 65%/$1.8B 12 rigs Delaware Second Bone/Wolfcamp A 1.2-1.5 MBOE EURs, AI drilling 15% faster, electric fracs; Bakken 15%/$400M 14k laterals 85% NGLs 22% IRR; GoM 15%/$400M Lobster/Marlin tie-backs NPV10 $500M 40% IRR; int'l 5%/$150M Namibia/CCUS. Returns 25%+ IRR, $55 WTI FCF breakeven, Apex Edge AI lifts recovery 10%, CCUS for 45Q.

Midstream generated $850 million EBITDA up 18% YoY: volumes 2.8 MMbbl/d crude, 4.2 Bcf/d gas, 450 Mbbl/d NGLs up 14% YoY 88% utilization. Crude 65% Permian via Longhorn 750 Mbbl/d 95% full to Nederland exports; gas Haynesville 1.8 Bcf/d 95% take-pay, Appalachia MVP 1.1 Bcf/d; NGLs Mont Belvieu 120 Mbbl/d ethane. Permian efficiencies/LNG ramps drove growth. Revenue $1.2B 92% fee-based 72% margins OpEx $1.85/bbl. Capex $2.5B: Matterhorn 400 Mbbl/d, Mont Belvieu #4 100 Mbbl/d, Haynesville South 1.2 Bcf/d 85% committed. Q4 volumes 2.9/4.4, EBITDA $825-875M.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Patel for an operational update.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, Mike. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 525,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought the Shenzi North tie-backs online, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives, with LOE efficiencies and AI predictive maintenance.

Now I will turn it over to David Kwon for an update on our exploration activities.

David Kwon: Thank you, Lisa. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Delaware and are planning to drill 25 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio, building on our fiscal 2023 proved additions of 285 MMBOE for a 142% RRR on 201 MMBOE production, organic 119%. Extensions/discoveries 177 MMBOE 62%, revisions 63 MMBOE 22%, improved recovery 34 MMBOE 12%. Up 24% YoY, 78% success rate. Permian 142 MMBOE 50% 132% organic 10+ year inventory; Eagle Ford 57 MMBOE 20% 115%; Bakken 43 MMBOE 15% 108% Three Mile 18 MMBOE; GoM 28 MMBOE 10% 95% Thunder Horse; int'l 15 MMBOE 5% 85% Stabroek/Johan. Reserves 2.8 BBOE 14-year life, F&D $12.50/boe half industry. AI modeling/Schlumberger Delfi 25% certainty, 4D seismic 200 MMBOE, frac innovations IP 1,500 BOE/d, CO2 EOR 12% uplift. 400-500 MMBOE inventory 70% oil $40-50 breakeven.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Elena Vasquez to discuss our marketing strategy.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, David. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for our NGL products in the Gulf Coast market area, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen our relationships with existing customers. The impact of these efforts on tolling revenue and export realizations is significant, aligning with midstream expansions capturing Permian outflows.

I will now turn it over to Tom Reilly to discuss our sustainability efforts.

Tom Reilly: Thank you, Elena. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and operating in a sustainable manner. We have made significant progress on reducing our greenhouse gas emissions, achieving a 35% Scope 1/2 intensity cut by 2030 from 2019's 18 kg CO2e/boe baseline, net-zero ops by 2050, SBTi-validated. H1 2024 absolute Scope 1/2 down 17% YoY to 12.4 Mmt CO2e, intensity 14.1 kg/boe down 22%, methane 0.18% beating 2025 target early, top quartile. Permian 45% production flaring 0.4% via infra 120 scf/D/boe, three Delaware systems 15 Bcf capture $45M EBITDA, GHGSat LDAR 1,200 leaks 25,000 mt saved. North Sea Magnus shore power 350,000 mt cut, Rosebank all-electric. Middle East QatarEnergy CCUS 1.2 Mmt H1 to 5 Mtpa, solvent capture 90% <$40/ton. APEX AI/Palantir 85% leak prediction, VRUs 80% Permian 95% recovery, hybrid rigs 25% fuel cut. Low-emission barrels $2/bbl premium Shell RSG deal, IRA $150M 45Q, 40% non-EU mix. $2.5B ESG capex 15% upstream, Sustainalytics 72/100.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on debt levels, net debt, and leverage ratios?

John Ramirez: Good morning, Alex. Mike covered this extensively earlier, but to recap, our deleveraging is on track with net debt at $12.4 billion and 1.6x leverage, positioning us strongly.

Operator: Our next question comes from Jordan Lee with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Jordan Lee: Good morning. What are your expectations for EBITDA YoY change and key drivers?

Mike Chen: Good morning, Jordan. We highlighted the 42% Q2 growth to $2.1 billion from pricing, volumes, and efficiencies, guiding FY $8.5-9.0 billion.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Energy Capital Partners. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Good morning. Could you please provide more color on proved reserves additions, reserve replacement ratio, and organic growth?

Lisa Patel: Good morning, Sarah. David touched on this, but to elaborate fully, our 2023 additions of 285 MMBOE gave 142% RRR organically 119%, detailed regionally and technically as outlined, supporting long-term FCF growth.

Operator: Our next question comes from Chris Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Chris Patel: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

David Kwon: Thanks, Chris. The exploration successes bolster our inventory to 10+ years, enabling sustained 8% CAGR without dilution, focusing on high-return Tier 1 acreage.

Operator: Our next question comes from Maria Gonzalez with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Maria Gonzalez: What is the outlook for the new NGL products in the coming years?

Elena Vasquez: Good morning, Maria. Strong demand and expansions like Mont Belvieu position NGLs for 10%+ volume growth, capturing export booms and premium pricing.

Operator: Our next question comes from Kevin Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Kevin Wong: Could you elaborate on your sustainability targets?

Tom Reilly: Good morning, Kevin. We're exceeding emissions reductions ahead of schedule with specific initiatives across basins, turning ESG into a competitive advantage as detailed.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to John Ramirez for closing remarks.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q2 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
